items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 27 at 3:32AM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
Snow will increase in intensity this afternoon. Winds begin easterly
this morning but do shift to the west in the afternoon with peak
gusts upwards of 40 mph. The combination of snow and wind will
result in reduced visibility below 1 mile at times, especially
between 3PM and 10PM. Expect additional snow accumulations between 1
and 3 inches.

The steadiest snow and strongest wind will end by midnight with
improving conditions thereafter.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 27 at 3:32AM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
Snow and wind will be most prevalent this morning. East winds
will gust upwards of 35 mph in Gambell through 9AM and weaken
quickly thereafter. There will be lowered visibility down to 1
mile this morning. Periods of snow continue at times through
Saturday but will be lessening in intensity with gradual
improvement expected this afternoon through Saturday.

items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 27 at 3:08AM AKST until November 27 at 10:00PM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Blowing Snow. Winds gusting as high as 45 mph.

* WHERE...Central Beaufort Sea Coast.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM AKST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Areas of blowing snow could significantly reduce
visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Strong winds will blow snow already on the
ground to create areas of low visibility near the surface. Winds
are significantly weaker farther inland.
items.instruction:
Use caution while traveling, especially in open areas. Visit
511.alaska.gov or call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.

items.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 27 at 3:08AM AKST until November 27 at 10:00PM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Periods of blizzard conditions. Winds gusting as high as 45
mph.

* WHERE...Point Thomson.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM AKST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Areas of blowing snow could significantly reduce
visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Strong winds will blow snow already on the
ground to create areas of low visibility near the surface. No
significant visibility reductions are expected at Barter
Island/Kaktovik due to open water limiting the availability of
blowable snow to the east.
items.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency.

items.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 26 at 1:04PM AKST until November 27 at 8:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:

20 mph gusting to 25 to 30 mph.

* WHERE...Homer Spit.

* WHEN...2 PM to 8 PM Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Water and light debris could wash over portions of the
Homer Spit Road. Minor beach erosion is possible.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 26 at 11:59AM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
Periods of snow become increasingly likely through Thursday as a
front approaches the coast. Southeast winds gusting up to 35 mph
shift southerly and peak up to 40 mph late Friday. The
combination of falling snow and strong winds are expected to lead
to periods of reduced visibility due to blowing snow, with
visibilities falling to 1 mile or less at times. Total snow
accumulations of 1 to 3 inches expected through Friday night. The
heaviest snow is expected near Cape Romanzof including Chevak,

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 26 at 11:59AM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
Periods of snow are likely Thursday and Friday with southeast
winds gusting up to 45 mph. This will likely result in lowered
visibility to 1 mile or less at times. Temperatures will be
hovering near 32 degrees which means blowing snow will only be
expected when it is actively snowing. Total snow accumulations
around 2 to 4 inches expected through Friday evening.
